beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Pavan Majji, a backend software engineer. When an error shows up, the habit is to paste it into a chatbot and ask how to fix it. The better question is which log lines prove the cause.

show.event: backspaces 'how do I fix it' → 'which log lines prove it' on the spoken correction

props.text:
What caused this error,
and how do I fix it?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive fix-it question and corrects it to the real one: which log lines prove the cause.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Root cause: the failure that started the problem. Source grounding: every claim points to the exact text it came from. A prompt contract: a fixed answer format a program can check.

terms.meaning: the failure that started the problem
every claim points to the exact text it came from
a fixed answer format a program can check

beats.narration_text: This is my final project, Cite the Line. Nothing in it is built yet. This film is the plan.

beats.narration_text: It will be a command-line tool. You give it the logs from a failing backend service, and it names the likely cause, pointing at the exact lines that support it.

beats.narration_text: To test it, I'll build a small service with FastAPI and Postgres in Docker, and break it on purpose: a slowed database, a bad config, a failing dependency. Each break gives real logs with a known cause.

beats.narration_text: Claude Code, run from a script, will read each incident and answer in a fixed format: one cause from a short list, plus the line numbers it relied on. That format is the prompt contract.

shot.motion_claim: Log pages slide into an open box labelled 'Claude Code'; a slip comes out with a cause pill and line-number marks, labelled 'contract'; a small 'constructed sketch' tag in the lower-right corner.

beats.narration_text: Then a plain checker, with no AI in it, will test every answer. Do the cited lines exist? Is the cause the known one? Each incident will run three times, to see if the answer holds.

beats.narration_text: Tools like this already exist. I read the documentation for Datadog's Bits AI SRE, which proposes root causes inside Datadog's paid platform. Its accuracy is reported by Datadog, and I can't re-check it myself.

beats.narration_text: Mine will be small and open: plain log files, incidents with known answers, and a public record of where it was wrong. It's not a competitor. It's a test bench anyone can re-check.

beats.narration_text: Then they click one incident and see the log, the diagnosis, and the checker's verdict, side by side, with no setup needed.

beats.narration_text: If it works, a reviewer could fairly conclude that I test model output instead of trusting it. They shouldn't conclude it works on real production logs. It will only be tested on incidents I made.

beats.narration_text: One thing it will never do is act. No restarts, no rollbacks. It only diagnoses and cites.

beats.narration_text: The first piece I'll make run is a single slowed-database incident, end to end. Its log, diagnosis and verdict will be committed with a date, so anyone can see it ran.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk is that I write every incident, so the test could be too easy. If the logs announce the answer, a high score means nothing.

beats.narration_text: So I'll add cases where the loudest error is not the real cause, and cases with no clear answer. If scores still look too good, I'll try a simple keyword script, and say so if it does as well.
